text: Vacuous assertion in the exam, inherited from the Proof text. tests/availability.test.ts:444-452 ("leg (e) [M5]: the mask string compares equal before and after the calls") captures `${DEFAULT_MASK}` / `${mondayOneAm}` and re-compares them after three projectToUtc calls. Because `Mask` is `export type Mask = string` (src/types.ts:11), JavaScript string immutability makes this pass for any implementation, including one that internally corrupts its working copy

the behaviour it names ('projectToUtc does not mutate the mask it was given') cannot be falsified. It leaves no criterion unverified in substance, since the rest of leg (e) pins the actual outputs, so this is advisory only. The fix is in the plan's leg (e) wording, not in this diff: to make it bite, the leg would have to pin an observable consequence, e.g. that a second projectToUtc call on the same mask returns a deep-equal array to the first. Not proposing a patch on the exam path, since editing it would drop a peer-written assertion.

unverified: the second half of the Claim, 'two people who share no hours are never treated as able to meet', is a cross-task property. This diff establishes only that `feasible` (src/core/availability.ts:206-208) returns false for disjoint projections

nothing here shows the matcher actually consults it before forming a pairing, since src/core/matching.ts is sibling task 3's file and is not touched. What would settle it: task 3's exam asserting the matcher rejects an infeasible candidate pair, and task 13's simulated month, which the Acceptance block already names as the integration-spanning exam.

`compose` builds the composed `reads` from every strategy handed in, not from the weighted parts: `for (const strategy of strategies)` at src/core/strategies.ts (the `const reads: Signal[] = []` loop). M5 says `reads` is "the deduplicated union of its parts' reads", and the task's Context says compose "ignores a strategy the weights do not name" — an unnamed strategy contributes nothing to the score but still widens the declared reads, so the composed strategy declares signals no scoring part consumes. The exam does not catch this because leg (e)'s reads case names both stubs in the weights (tests/strategies.test.ts, "composed reads are the deduplicated union of its parts' reads"), and the only test that exercises an unnamed strategy ("compose ignores a strategy the weights do not name") asserts on the score, not on `reads`. Effect is a superset of signals passed to buildContext, benign at runtime, so this is advisory rather than blocking.

`bruteForceOptimal` returns `Math.max(search(0), greedySum)` (src/core/matching.ts:107-108) rather than the recursion's own answer. Because the greedy set is by construction one of the disjoint compatible sets the recursion enumerates, this clamp is a no-op in exact arithmetic — but it makes the exam's six-fixture leg `expect(gap).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0)` (tests/matching.test.ts:437) unfalsifiable: if the recursion ever under-counted, the clamp would paper over it and that assertion would still pass. The exam's own fixture design already removes the float motive it cites (scores are k/1024 and at most five are summed, so every sum is exact in IEEE754, as the comment at tests/matching.test.ts:408-412 says). M4's substantive pins (optimal 1.7 vs greedy 1.05 on the four-member table, 0.4 on the two-member pool) do exercise the recursion for real, so this does not leave M4 unverified — it only weakens the property leg. Dropping the clamp would make that leg bite.

unverified: `ProposedPair.fresh` is produced by the Interfaces slot and its semantics are fixed by Context ("`fresh` is true when no record in `history` names both ids"), and it is implemented at src/core/matching.ts:175-181, but no Machine clause and no Proof leg names it, and tests/matching.test.ts passes `NO_HISTORY` everywhere — every assertion in the exam would still pass if `fresh` were hardcoded `true`. `tsc --noEmit` settles the field's presence and type, nothing settles its value. What would settle it: one case in tests/matching.test.ts that matches a two-member pool against a history containing a `PairingRecord` whose `members` are those two ids (in both orders) and asserts `fresh === false`, plus a pool with an unrelated record asserting `fresh === true`.

Claim-vs-Machine gap in the pull-forward reconnect path. The Claim promises "when I have met everyone it reconnects me and says so", and M5 delivers the "says so" half only for the `pick`-proposal path: `pick` proposes a repeat, neither side has a stranger, novelty `'reconnect'` plus a `'met-everyone'` notice per side. The Context algorithm's step (3) describes the other reconnect path -- "if no stranger exists anywhere, pair with the soonest-eligible in-reach repeat as `'reconnect'`" -- with no notice at all, and M3 asks only for the pairing and the `pullForward` entry. src/core/pool.ts:189-195 transcribes that faithfully: the step-3 reconnect calls `accept(m, partner, 'reconnect')` and pushes `partner.id` onto `pullForward` without emitting any notice, so a member reconnected by pull-forward is told nothing. Exam leg (c)'s second case (tests/pool.test.ts:439-452) asserts the pairing, its novelty and `pullForward` and says nothing about notices, so the exam cannot distinguish either way. Not blocking: the diff satisfies every Machine clause as written, and the omission is in the task's own Context and Machine text rather than in the submission. Flagging it for Task 13, which is where the notice would surface to a member. If the intent is that this path also speaks, the plan needs a Machine clause and a leg extension

the implementation change would then be a two-line addition inside src/core/pool.ts pushing a `'met-everyone'` notice for `m` (and, arguably, for the pulled-forward partner) carrying `partnerId` and `metAt(m.id, partner.id)` as `lastPairedAt`.

Three of leg (a)'s four ineligibility cases exercise only the pool filter, not the pull-forward candidate filter, because the plan pins the other member's `eligibleAt` to `now`. In tests/pool.test.ts:351-363 the paused, `needsAck` and `openPairingMembers` cases all build `other` with `eligibleAt: NOW`, which fails the pull-forward reach predicate's `other.eligibleAt > now` leg (src/core/pool.ts:177) before the `!other.needsAck` / `!openPairingMembers.has` / `state === 'active'` legs are ever consulted. Those three tests do bite on `inPool` (src/core/pool.ts:84-85): dropping the state, `needsAck` or open-pairing check there puts `other` in the pool, `stubPick(["lone","other"])` proposes the pair, and the pair is accepted as `'fresh'`, so the tests fail. They just leave the corresponding guards in the reach filter (src/core/pool.ts:173-176) unverified, so that redundancy is dead weight as far as the exam can tell. The fourth case, `eligibleAt: now + pullForwardMaxMs + 1`, does bite on the reach filter's window bound. No change asked of the submission: the exam transcribes the plan's leg (a) verbatim, and the gap is in the leg's chosen fixtures. Setting `eligibleAt: NOW + 1 * DAY` on the paused / needsAck / open cases would close it.

src/core/scheduling.ts:231 — `enterLocked` carries a silent fallback for `proposedStartUtc === null`: it still returns state `locked` with `lockedStartUtc: null`, emits no `room-open`/`room-close`/`follow-up` schedules, and says `locked` with no `vars`. That output contradicts M4 (entering `locked` yields the three schedules) and the Context line pinning `locked` to `{ start }`, and it is the one path through the module where a legal-looking transition produces a state the app (Task 13) cannot act on — the `{start}` placeholder in the `locked` copy would render unfilled. The branch is unreachable from `initialState` (only `one_confirmed` + `confirm` enters `locked`, and `one_confirmed` is only reachable via a proposal), so no exam leg touches it and nothing is unverified

it is a defensive path that should refuse rather than degrade. Suggested: replace the early return with `throw new IllegalTransition('cannot lock without a standing proposal')`. The exam is unaffected — `REPS.one_confirmed` sets `proposedStartUtc: START`.

tests/scheduling.test.ts:565-566 — the two assertions closing leg (a) (`expect(observedLegal.length).toBe(13)` and `expect(observedLegal.slice().sort()).toEqual(Object.keys(M1).slice().sort())`) are tautologies over the test's own fixture: `sawLegal` is set from `rule = M1[key]` being present, never from anything `transition` returned, so both still pass with the entire implementation deleted. The leg they name — "the count of legal combinations found is exactly 13" — is nonetheless genuinely established by the loop above them, since a 14th legal pair would make one of the 50 off-table combinations fail its target-or-throw assertion. No criterion is left unverified, so this is advisory only: to make the count assertion load-bearing, set `sawLegal` from the observed outcome (e.g. `if (outcomeLabel(rep, ev) !== 'IllegalTransition') sawLegal = true`) rather than from `rule`.

unverified: src/core/scheduling.ts:285 — `repropose` reuses the `proposal` copy key for the say emitted when a timezone change moves a locked call. The task pins say keys for `propose`, `counter`, the first `confirm`, the locking `confirm`, the three released entries and `follow-up`, but is silent on the `tz-repropose` say, and no exam leg asserts it, so the diff cannot settle whether this is the intended key — `src/types.ts:267-268` carries `tz-changed-locked-call` and `pick-another-time`, which read as the keys written for this moment. What would settle it: Task 13's wiring of the tz-change path, or Task 10's copy defaults, showing which key the rendered message is meant to come from. If `proposal` is wrong the correction is a one-word change here, but it is only visible once the app renders it.

Coverage gap on a Context requirement: the Context slot requires RFC 5545 escaping of commas, semicolons and newlines in SUMMARY, DESCRIPTION and LOCATION. `escapeText` at src/core/calendar.ts (the `escapeText` helper used by `ics`) implements it correctly, but no assertion in tests/calendar.test.ts exercises it — the fixture `EVENT` has no comma, semicolon, backslash or newline in any of the three fields, so deleting `escapeText` and inlining the raw values leaves the whole exam green. This is not one of the Proof legs, so it is advisory, not blocking. A test over an event whose summary, description and threadUrl carry the special characters would close it.

unverified: the Context states the default window `{ minDays: 3, maxDays: 10 }` is what Task 13 passes, and that `shared` is the output of Task 1's `sharedHours`. Neither seam is touched by this diff — `proposeSlots` takes the window and the number list as parameters and imports nothing. Task 13's simulated month is what would settle that the caller supplies hour-aligned UTC starts and the 3-to-10-day window
nothing in this patch can.

`MemoryJobStore.get(id)` (src/jobs/memory-store.ts:66) is added but never called by anything in this tree, and leg (g) in tests/jobs.test.ts:441-447 explicitly works around its absence: its comment claims "Job.state is not readable through JobStore" and then observes M7's "the job stays done" indirectly (not pending, not due, not completable). That indirect trio cannot distinguish `done` from `cancelled`, which is exactly the distinction M7 names, and the direct observation is already sitting on the class. Either assert the state through `get` or drop the unused method.

unverified: M6's stated purpose ("the reference semantics the SQLite store has to match", src/jobs/memory-store.ts:8-9) is a cross-task claim this diff cannot settle — nothing here compares MemoryJobStore against Task 9's `src/storage/sqlite.ts`. Task 13's simulated month running this Scheduler over the SQLite store is what would settle it.

Test name overclaims: `tests/storage.test.ts` leg (a) case "SCHEMA_SQL is the eight CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS statements, in order" never asserts the order. It checks `length === 8`, that each statement matches /CREATE\s+TABLE\s+IF\s+NOT\s+EXISTS/i, and that the joined text contains each of the eight names — all of which still pass if SCHEMA_SQL is shuffled. The Context clause it encodes ("`SCHEMA_SQL` is the list of `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` statements run on open, in order") is therefore untested. No Machine clause or Proof leg names the order, so this is advisory rather than blocking, and the implementation does follow the Context order (guilds, members, pairings, pairing_members, proposals, confirmations, outcomes, jobs) — the exam just does not pin it.

Silent fabrication of a member id: `src/storage/sqlite.ts` `toPairing` builds `members: [ids[0] ?? '', ids[1] ?? '']` from the surviving `pairing_members` rows, so after `forgetMember(g,'m1')` a `getPairing`/`openPairings`/`pairingsOf` read of that pairing returns `members: ['m2', '']` — an empty string typed as a `MemberId`. Downstream consumers that iterate `PairingRecord.members` (matching, scheduling, the Task 13 month) would treat `''` as a person. The exam acknowledges this at the M5 leg (e) case "the partner's row, the pairing and the partner's outcome are untouched", which excludes `members` from its comparison, so it is disclosed rather than hidden. The fix does not lie inside this task's FILES: the task's Context fixes `pairings` to (id, guild_id, thread_id, voice_channel_id, state, novelty, created_at) with no member columns, so the pair genuinely cannot be reconstructed once a membership row is deleted. Settling it means either §6 keeping the member ids on the pairing row, or `types.ts` letting `PairingRecord.members` express an absent side.

Global constraint "Every table has a `guild_id` column and every query is scoped by it" is not met by two statements, and cannot be met as the interface stands: `dueJobs(now)` queries `WHERE state = 'pending' AND run_at <= ?` and `completeJob(id)` queries `WHERE id = ?`, both unscoped. Neither method takes a `guildId` — `JobStore` in `src/types.ts:176-185` declares `dueJobs(now: number)` and `completeJob(id: string)`, which is deliberate (the scheduler ticks across guilds and job ids are globally unique), so no edit inside `src/storage/sqlite.ts` can scope them without diverging from the consumed interface. The constraint carries no `Check:` the driver ran, so this is my reading of its prose: as written it admits no exception for the cross-guild job sweep. Every other read and write in the file is guild-scoped, and the eight tables all carry `guild_id` (verified by the passing leg (a) cases).

Global constraint "A `Mask` is exactly 168 characters of `0` or `1` ... any function given another length throws an `Error` whose message contains `168`" is unenforced at the storage boundary: `upsertMember` writes `row.mask` into `availability_mask` with no length check, so a malformed mask persists silently and reads back malformed. The constraint has no `Check:` command behind it and I read it as aimed primarily at the mask functions of `src/core/availability.ts`, so this is advisory — but `upsertMember` is a function given a mask, and a one-line guard there (`if (row.mask.length !== 168) throw new Error(...168...)`) would both satisfy the strict reading and keep a bad row out of the database. No existing exam case would break: every mask the exam writes is the 168-character `MASK`.

Duplicated predicate in `src/storage/sqlite.ts` `cancelJobs`: the same four-term WHERE clause (`guild_id`, `kind`, `ref_id`, `state = 'pending'`) is written twice, once to count the rows and once to update them, so a future change to the predicate has to be made in both places to stay correct. `completeJob` has the same shape (SELECT the state, then UPDATE). bun:sqlite's `.run()` returns `{ changes }`, so each could be one statement whose own result gives the count — `cancelJobs` returning `changes` and `completeJob` returning `changes === 1` after `UPDATE ... WHERE id = ? AND state = 'pending'`. Behaviour is correct as written and the M6 leg (f) cases pass
this is code quality only.

Scope beyond the task: `guildTables` in src/config/file-store.ts (patch lines ~279-291) accepts two shapes the task never asks for — a single `[guilds]` table and a lone guild written at top level, recognized by the `GUILD_KEYS` sniff. The Context slot pins the file shape to `[[guilds]]` tables, and neither extra branch is exercised by tests/config.test.ts, so it is untested tolerance carrying a silent-acceptance risk (a document with a stray top-level `copy` key is read as a guild and then throws a 'missing required field guild_id' error that names the wrong problem). Not blocking: the required `[[guilds]]` path is correct and proven green. Suggested fix is to drop the `isTable(guilds)` and `GUILD_KEYS.some(...)` branches, or add a leg covering them.

Reading of the prose global constraint 'No user-facing string in `src/` or `config.example.toml` contains ... any mention of KmikeyM, shares or votes': config.example.toml line 12 (patch line 12) reads 'nothing is shared between them'. I read the constraint as barring the equity sense of 'shares', which this is not — it is the verb, about per-guild data isolation — and the driver's `Check:` for this constraint (`grep -rniE 'kmikeym|shareholder|experiment'`) exits 0, as does exam leg (e). Flagging only because the word survives a future stricter §11 sweep only by that reading
'nothing is carried between them' removes the ambiguity at zero cost.

Footprint: `tsconfig.json` is modified (adds `"skipLibCheck": true`) and is outside this task's FILES (src/adapters/discord/commands.ts, components.ts, zones.ts, tests/discord-commands.test.ts). It is not a sibling-owned path, so this is minor, not blocking, but the change is repo-wide: it relaxes `bunx tsc --noEmit` — the Global Constraints `Check:` command every other task is graded by — for all declaration files, not just discord.js's. It is plausibly required (discord.js's shipped .d.ts under this tree's `strict` + `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` baseline), and the driver's check exits 0 with it. If it is not required, revert it
if it is, it belongs in the seed/baseline task rather than arriving inside an adapter task, since a later task that reverts or conflicts on tsconfig.json silently re-reds this one.

Unrequired surface in `src/adapters/discord/zones.ts`: `isKnownZone()` and `AUTOCOMPLETE_LIMIT`, and in `src/adapters/discord/components.ts`: `AVAILABILITY_PRESETS`, are exported but named by neither the Produces list nor any Machine clause, and nothing in this patch calls `isKnownZone` or `AVAILABILITY_PRESETS`. They are small and plausibly staged for the Task 13 gateway adapter, so this is advisory only — but if no sibling Consumes them they are dead exports on the adapter's public surface and should be dropped or made module-private. Separately, `zoneSuggestions` clamps a caller-supplied `limit` down to 25 (`Math.min(Math.floor(limit), AUTOCOMPLETE_LIMIT)`) rather than the Context's literal "cut to `limit`"
the clamp is the right behaviour for Discord's cap and M2 only requires `<= 25`, but a caller asking for 40 gets 25 with no signal.

unverified: the Claim's end-to-end half — "I type /join, start typing my city, and the timezone fills itself in" — is not settled by this diff. The patch produces the command JSON with `autocomplete: true` and the pure `zoneSuggestions()` list, but nothing here registers the commands over REST, answers an `APPLICATION_COMMAND_AUTOCOMPLETE` interaction, or renders `availabilityMenu`/`daysSelect`/`hoursSelect` into discord.js components

that wiring is the gateway adapter's (Task 13), and the acceptance text already names Task 13's simulated month as the integration-spanning exam. What would settle it: Task 13's exam driving an autocomplete interaction through the adapter and asserting the choices come back from `zoneSuggestions`, and a button-press round-trip through `parseCustomId`. Every Machine clause M1-M6 this task does own is pinned by a named assertion in tests/discord-commands.test.ts and green in EXAM EVIDENCE.

concern: out-of-FILES: tsconfig.json gained "skipLibCheck": true. It is not in my FILES and not in any sibling's. It is unavoidable for the proof `bunx tsc --noEmit`: node_modules/@sapphire/shapeshift (a discord.js dependency) imports `InspectOptionsStylized` from `util`, which bun-types does not export, so the first module in this repo to import discord.js turns tsc red on a library file nobody owns. skipLibCheck is the narrow fix and does not weaken checking of src/ or tests/. If a sibling adds the same line the text is identical.

concern: plan-defect: the task names three source files but never says which of the eleven produced symbols lives in which, while the peer writes tests/discord-commands.test.ts blind. I resolved it by giving each symbol its natural home and having commands.ts `export * from './zones'` and `export * from './components'`, so every produced symbol resolves from src/adapters/discord/commands.ts as well. zones.ts and components.ts import nothing from commands.ts, so there is no cycle. This is a disclosure, not a park: all legs pass.

concern: The `matchbook` group carries `.setDefaultMemberPermissions(PermissionFlagsBits.ManageGuild)` so the admin commands are admin-only per spec s7. This adds a `default_member_permissions` field to that command's JSON but changes none of the names, types, `required` or `autocomplete` values leg (a) reads.
unverified: the Claim ("clone, edit one TOML file, docker compose up, and I have a working bot in under ten minutes") is never exercised end to end. Every Proof `Run:` is a grep over text

no command builds the image or starts the service, and the two files the Quickstart's happy path actually needs are absent at BASE and sibling-owned: `src/main.ts` (Task 14), which both `CMD ["bun", "run", "src/main.ts"]` in Dockerfile:14 and `bun run src/main.ts --check-config config.toml` in README.md:168 name, and `config.example.toml` (Task 10), which `cp config.example.toml config.toml` in README.md:151 names. This is not a missing dependency edge: every Machine criterion M1-M7 is satisfiable, and is satisfied, from this task's own four files. What would settle it is Task 13's integration exam plus one `docker build .` smoke on the merged tree, which would also settle the one build-time risk this diff carries: `WORKDIR /app` with `RUN bun install` assumes the `oven/bun:1` image's default build user can write `/app`. If that image sets a non-root default user, `bun install` fails on the layer
a `USER root` before the install, or a `WORKDIR` under the image's own home, is the fix. I could not check the image's Dockerfile from this sandbox.

README.md:165-173 breaks the Docker-only premise it just established. The invite step is written as a bare host command, `bun run src/main.ts --check-config config.toml`, but the Quickstart never has the reader install Bun, and the whole point of the compose file is that Docker is the only tooling needed. It is also sequenced after `docker compose up`, so the reader's first `up` starts a bot that is in no server yet, and is then told to run `docker compose up` "again". Naming `--check-config` here is authorized by the task's Context, so this is copy, not scope: run it through the service instead, e.g. `docker compose run --rm matchbook bun run src/main.ts --check-config config.toml` (config.toml is already bind mounted read-only), and move the paragraph above the `docker compose up` line so the invite happens before the first start.

README.md:145 says "Four commands and one file to edit", but the fence directly below it at README.md:148-155 holds six commands (`git clone`, `cd`, `cp`, `$EDITOR`, `export`, `docker compose up`). The task's M3 pins four specific lines, which the block has in order, so the proof is unaffected
the sentence is just wrong about its own code block. "A handful of commands and one file to edit", or a count of six, fixes it.
